extraction_notes.boundary_rule_applied: NO-UNIT — the directory contains essentially no prose, so neither clause of the boundary rule is satisfied: nothing REPORTS an incident and nothing DISCUSSES the concept. This is not a thin read standing in for a judgement. The directory holds numeric result files (marginal/joint distinctness, per-level counts, resample bands), six sixdim data dumps and four tagged TSVs that are machine-emitted term lists, fifteen tree-spec seed files and one seed pool whose only free text is generated corpus content (commitment/delta/summary fields), three captured request payloads whose long strings are the generation prompt, one harness script whose docstring describes what it captures, and two probe artifacts. I surveyed every JSON in the directory and both subdirectories for free-text fields rather than inferring absence from the file listing; the longest non-corpus prose string in the whole directory is a 127-character arm description.
extraction_notes.near_misses_recorded: Three things in this directory evidence defects without any prose reporting them, recorded so that this NO-UNIT is not mistaken for 'nothing here'. (1) A quarantine artifact listing 12 edges whose targets did not resolve to a canonical identifier, including one where the target is a misspelling of a sibling identifier — real repair-time evidence, written by a script, described nowhere. (2) A results field whose name states that 26 control-arm members are missing one of the five dimensions the comparison is computed over, carried as a bare integer alongside that comparison, with no note — INFERRED from the field name and the dimension list beside it, since there is no prose anywhere in the directory to confirm or deny it. (3) One stratum carries the verdict 'underpowered' at n=26 versus n=6, which is a declared scope limit rather than an incident. None of these is prose, so none of them is a UNIT under the rule as written.
extraction_notes.escalation: FLAGGED FOR THE OPERATOR, not decided by me. The boundary rule partitions documents into REPORTS-an-instance and DISCUSSES-the-concept; both presuppose prose. This directory is a third case the rule does not name — a defect present only as a machine-written artifact, with no narrative anywhere. I applied the rule as written (NO-UNIT) rather than extending it, because extending it here would be the extractor deciding what counts as a report. The consequence for the escape check is worth stating plainly: a directory carrying no prose cannot be a keyword-proxy hit in either direction, so it tests the proxy's recall only in the weak sense that there was nothing to recall.
extraction_notes.operator_ruling_2026_08_11: RULED: NO-UNIT stands, and the escalation was correct that the boundary rule does not name this case. Recorded as a THIRD CATEGORY — outside the frame rather than inside it — because the census searches prose, and a directory with no prose can be neither a keyword-proxy hit nor a miss. Counting it as an ordinary NO-UNIT would inflate the precision denominator with a directory the proxy was never able to see. Same reasoning as the empty untracked directory: not a defect in the figure, a defect in the frame.
